subject.title: [Feature] Allow per-binding tool restrictions (tools.deny) in route/ACP bindings

question: Should `bindings[].tools.allow/deny` become a supported security boundary for both route and ACP bindings, and what precedence should it have relative to global, agent, group, sender, subagent, and inherited policies?
rationale: This cannot be safely inferred from code alone because it adds a public config surface whose deny rules operators may rely on for access control, and a partial schema-only implementation was already closed as unsafe.

options.title: Implement end-to-end binding policy
options.body: Add the new binding config only with runtime enforcement, precedence tests, docs, and route/ACP coverage proving denied tools are unavailable for matched bindings.

options.title: Defer to existing sender policy
options.body: Keep `bindings[]` focused on routing and document `tools.toolsBySender` plus agent-specific policies as the supported restriction surfaces for now.

options.title: Scope to route bindings first
options.body: Allow only normal route bindings initially and leave ACP binding policy for a separate reviewed contract if ACP session semantics need different precedence.

recommendation.title: Implement end-to-end binding policy
recommendation.body: Add the new binding config only with runtime enforcement, precedence tests, docs, and route/ACP coverage proving denied tools are unavailable for matched bindings.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent scoped capability profile and routing history make this the best available owner for the product/security boundary decision.
